quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Sofia and her brother are going camping this weekend. They pack a tent, sleeping bags, a flashlight, and enough water for two days. Sofia also brings a small first-aid kit, just in case. By Friday night, everything is in the car.
options: How to Choose the Best Flashlight
quests.hint: List the objects in the passage, then ask what job they are all doing.
quests.explanation: The tent, water, and first-aid kit are all items for one trip. A title about only the flashlight is too small, and a hike is never mentioned.
quests.whyThisTitle: Every item and the Friday-night detail belong to preparing for the trip, not to any single object.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Once each term, teachers meet with parents to talk about how students are doing. The teacher shows examples of the child's work and explains where the child is strong. Parents can ask questions and suggest ways to help at home. Each meeting lasts about fifteen minutes.
options: A Guide to Choosing a New School
quests.hint: Who is talking to whom in this passage, and how often?
quests.explanation: The passage describes a regular conversation between teacher and parent. Reading at home is only one thing that might come up in it.
quests.whyThisTitle: This title names the meeting that includes work samples, questions, and suggestions.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Birdwatching needs patience more than equipment. A pair of binoculars and a notebook are enough to begin. Sit quietly near trees or water and listen for songs before you look. Even a small park can show you a surprising number of birds.
quests.hint: Ask whether the passage is about one piece of equipment or about beginning the hobby.
quests.explanation: Binoculars and a notebook appear, but only as part of the beginner's kit. The passage as a whole tells a newcomer how to start.
quests.whyThisTitle: This choice covers the equipment, the technique, and the place, which together are the beginner's path into the hobby.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Tomas's first week at the design studio was busy. He met his team, learned where supplies were kept, and sat in on two meetings. On Friday, his manager asked how he was doing, and Tomas said he finally felt at home.
options: How to Choose a Career in Design
quests.hint: Look at how Tomas feels at the start of the week and at the end.
quests.explanation: Meeting people, finding things, and attending meetings are all parts of getting used to a workplace. The Friday chat is only the final scene.
quests.whyThisTitle: The passage follows Tomas from unfamiliar surroundings to feeling at home, which is what settling in means.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Many travelers on a small budget stay in hostels. A bed in a shared room costs much less than a hotel room, and there is usually a kitchen guests can use. Lockers keep bags safe. Guests also meet people from other countries in the common room.
options: Meeting Travelers in a Common Room
Staying in a Hostel on a Budget
quests.correctAnswer: Staying in a Hostel on a Budget
quests.hint: Notice what most of the details have in common: they all describe what a hostel offers.
quests.explanation: Low prices, a kitchen, lockers, and a common room all describe hostel stays. Meeting people is one feature, so it is too narrow to be the title.
quests.whyThisTitle: Cost, kitchen, lockers, and social space all point to why hostels suit budget travelers.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Smoke alarms only work if their batteries are fresh. Once a month, press the test button and listen for a loud beep. Change the batteries every year, even if the alarm still sounds fine. Fire officers say a working alarm gives a family time to get out safely.
options: How Fire Trucks Reach a House
Replacing the Battery in a Clock
Keeping Smoke Alarms in Working Order
quests.correctAnswer: Keeping Smoke Alarms in Working Order
quests.hint: What action does the passage repeat with different timing?
quests.explanation: Monthly testing and yearly battery changes are two ways to keep the same device working. An escape route is related to fire safety, but it is not what this passage covers.
quests.whyThisTitle: The monthly test and yearly battery change both serve the goal of an alarm that works when needed.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Behind the apartment block, residents share a small garden. Each family has a wooden box for vegetables, and everyone takes turns watering. In summer, people trade extra tomatoes and beans. The garden gives neighbors a reason to talk and a bit of fresh food.
options: Living in a Large Apartment Block
quests.hint: Ask what the garden gives to the people, not only what grows in it.
quests.explanation: Boxes, watering turns, and trading vegetables show a garden run by a group. A title about tomatoes or planters would leave out the community side.
quests.whyThisTitle: The shared boxes, turns, and trading all show one garden used by neighbors together.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Ana had to give a five-minute talk in English class. She wrote a few key points on cards instead of a full script. Then she practiced in front of a mirror and timed herself. On the day, she felt nervous but knew what to say.
options: Making Cards to Learn New Words
Getting Ready for a Class Talk
quests.correctAnswer: Getting Ready for a Class Talk
quests.hint: Look for the event Ana is working toward, and list what she does before it.
quests.explanation: Cards, a mirror, and a timer are all preparation for one talk. Nervousness is mentioned, but the passage is mostly about what she did to get ready.
quests.whyThisTitle: The cards, the practice, and the timing are all preparation for the talk.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Most city subways use a rechargeable card. You touch it to the gate when you enter, and the fare comes off your balance. If the balance gets low, you can add money at a machine in the station or with a phone app. It saves you from buying a ticket for every trip.
options: Paying for the Subway with a Card
Finding Your Way Around a Station
Adding Money with a Phone App
quests.correctAnswer: Paying for the Subway with a Card
quests.hint: Ask how many separate parts of the card system the passage explains.
quests.explanation: Touching in, having the fare deducted, and adding money are all parts of one payment system. The phone app is only one way to top up.
quests.whyThisTitle: The passage covers using the card, being charged, and refilling it, so the title needs to cover paying overall.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: The public pool has a few simple rules. Everyone must shower before getting in. Children under eight need an adult in the water, and running on the deck is not allowed. Lifeguards are always on duty and will blow a whistle if someone breaks a rule.
options: Learning to Swim as an Adult
Safety Rules at the Public Pool
quests.correctAnswer: Safety Rules at the Public Pool
quests.hint: Look at the first sentence and the last one. What do the details in between illustrate?
quests.explanation: Showering, adult supervision, and no running are all rules, and the lifeguards are there to enforce them. The lifeguard job is a supporting detail, not the subject.
quests.whyThisTitle: Each detail is a rule or a way of enforcing one, so the title should name the rules.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: The school chess club meets after class on Tuesdays. Beginners learn how each piece moves, while stronger players teach simple plans. Every month, members hold a small tournament and the winner picks the next snack. Even students who lose say they enjoy it.
options: A Guide to Choosing After-School Snacks
School Chess Club for Every Skill Level
quests.correctAnswer: School Chess Club for Every Skill Level
quests.hint: Ask what kind of place the passage describes, and how the members treat each other.
quests.explanation: Lessons, monthly games, and a shared snack all show a club that welcomes different skill levels. The tournament is only one part of that picture.
quests.whyThisTitle: The mix of teaching, casual competition, and enjoyment describes a welcoming club rather than a contest.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Alex's kitchen drawer was full of tangled cords and old batteries. On Saturday, he emptied it onto the table and threw out what was broken. He kept only what he used, then placed small boxes inside to hold each type of item. Now he finds things in seconds.
options: Choosing Furniture for a Small Kitchen
quests.hint: Compare the drawer at the beginning with the drawer at the end.
quests.explanation: Emptying, discarding, and sorting into boxes are all stages of tidying one drawer. The title should describe that change.
quests.whyThisTitle: Sorting into boxes explains why the messy drawer now lets Alex find things quickly.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Every Thursday, volunteers sort donated food at the community center. They check dates on cans, pack boxes for families, and load them into vans. Some volunteers are students earning school credit, and others are retired neighbors. Together they prepare over a hundred boxes.
options: Donating Cans to a School Drive
quests.hint: The passage mentions several kinds of people and several tasks. What connects them?
quests.explanation: Checking dates, packing, and loading are tasks in one shared effort. Student credit and delivery are details inside that effort.
quests.whyThisTitle: Students and retirees are doing the same work, and the title names that work and its purpose.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Booking a medical appointment online takes only a few minutes. Choose the clinic, pick a day and time, and enter your phone number. The clinic sends a message to confirm and another reminder the day before. You can cancel with one click if plans change.
options: Finding the Best Doctor in Town
quests.hint: Follow the process from the first click to the day before the visit.
quests.explanation: Choosing a time, confirming, and receiving reminders belong to one booking process. Cancellation is mentioned only at the end.
quests.whyThisTitle: The steps from choosing a slot to getting reminders all describe how to book online.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: On Sundays, Grandma cooks a big lunch for the whole family. Cousins arrive with dishes to share, and the youngest children set the table. After eating, the adults talk while the kids play in the yard. Nobody remembers who did the dishes, but everyone remembers the stories.
options: Cooking a Large Meal Alone at Home
Playing Games in the Back Yard
Sunday Lunches with the Whole Family
quests.correctAnswer: Sunday Lunches with the Whole Family
quests.hint: Think about how the passage moves: before the meal, during it, and after.
quests.explanation: Cooking, sharing dishes, table setting, and stories all belong to one regular family gathering. Each other title picks out only a piece.
quests.whyThisTitle: From arrival to the yard and the stories, everything in the passage belongs to the weekly gathering.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Sara left her umbrella on the train. At the station, she went to the lost-and-found office and described it: blue, with a wooden handle. The clerk checked a shelf behind him and found it within minutes. Sara signed a form and took it home.
options: Signing Forms at a Train Station
quests.hint: Look for the problem at the start and the way it is solved.
quests.explanation: The passage moves from a lost item to a recovered one. The form and the train are only parts of that process.
quests.whyThisTitle: Describing the umbrella, the search, and the signature all lead to getting the umbrella back.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Each spring, Dana goes through her closet. She holds up every piece and asks herself if she wore it this year. Clothes she likes but no longer wears go into a donation bag. What is left fits neatly on the shelf, and she can see everything.
options: Clearing Out a Closet Each Spring
How to Choose Outfits for Work
quests.correctAnswer: Clearing Out a Closet Each Spring
quests.hint: Ask what Dana does with each piece of clothing and why.
quests.explanation: Holding up each item, deciding, and donating are steps in sorting through a closet. Donation is one result rather than the whole story.
quests.whyThisTitle: The yearly review of every piece explains both the donation bag and the neat shelf.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: When answering the office phone, start with a clear greeting and your name. Listen without interrupting, and write down important details like names and numbers. If you cannot help, say who can and offer to pass the call on. A polite voice gives callers a good first impression of the company.
options: A Guide to Choosing an Office Phone System
quests.hint: What kind of situation is being taught here, and who benefits from the advice?
quests.explanation: A greeting, careful listening, and offering to transfer the call are all ways of handling a work call well. Note-taking is only one part of that.
quests.whyThisTitle: Each piece of advice is about how to treat a caller, which the title names.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Salespeople suggest trying on running shoes in the afternoon, when feet are slightly larger. Wear the socks you will use for exercise and walk around the store. There should be about a thumb's width of space in front of the longest toe. A pair that feels comfortable right away is usually the right one.
options: Trying Shoes On in the Afternoon
quests.hint: Consider how many different tips there are, and what goal they share.
quests.explanation: Timing, socks, space, and comfort are all pieces of advice about fit. The afternoon tip is only one of them.
quests.whyThisTitle: The tips about timing, socks, and toe space together explain how to judge whether shoes fit.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: The town's lantern festival is held each autumn. Families make paper lanterns at home and carry them through the streets after sunset. Food stalls line the main road, and a band plays near the bridge. Thousands of visitors come to see the glowing parade.
options: Selling Food Along the Main Road
quests.hint: Ask what event ties together the lanterns, the food, and the band.
quests.explanation: Lanterns, food, and music are activities within one celebration. Each of the other titles takes just one activity.
quests.whyThisTitle: The lanterns, the stalls, and the crowds all describe a single yearly celebration.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Lucas used to forget his homework until the night before. Now he writes each assignment in a planner and marks the due date in red. Every Sunday he looks ahead and decides which days to start each task. His grades have improved, and he sleeps better.
options: Writing Due Dates in Red Ink
quests.hint: Compare what Lucas did before with what he does now.
quests.explanation: The planner, the red dates, and the Sunday check are methods for keeping up with work. Sleep and grades are results of that change.
quests.whyThisTitle: The passage is about the system Lucas built, and all his methods serve the goal of keeping up.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Passport photos have strict rules. The face must fill most of the picture, and the background must be plain white. Glasses should be removed, and the person should look straight ahead with a neutral expression. Many pharmacies take these photos, and they know the rules.
options: Choosing a Camera for Family Portraits
quests.hint: Look at what the passage tells you about the picture itself.
quests.explanation: Face size, background, glasses, and expression are all requirements for one kind of photo. The pharmacy mention is a practical tip at the end.
quests.whyThisTitle: The requirements about size, background, and expression are all about how a passport photo must look.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: The library's summer reading program starts in June. Children pick books from a special shelf and keep a record of every one they finish. After ten books, they earn a free ticket to the science museum. Librarians say the program helps children keep reading while school is closed.
options: Summer Reading for Children at the Library
quests.correctAnswer: Summer Reading for Children at the Library
quests.hint: The reward is exciting, but what is the reward for?
quests.explanation: The free ticket is a prize inside a larger program. The passage explains how the program works and why the library runs it.
quests.whyThisTitle: The program, its rules, and its goal of keeping children reading are all covered by the title.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: The sales team now keeps one shared calendar. Everyone adds meetings, trips, and vacation days, and each person can see who is free at a glance. Booking a meeting takes less time because nobody has to send several messages. The calendar has already cut down on double bookings.
options: Using a Shared Calendar at Work
Planning Vacation Days for the Year
quests.correctAnswer: Using a Shared Calendar at Work
quests.hint: Ask what tool the team adopted and what it changed.
quests.explanation: Adding events, seeing availability, and fewer double bookings all come from one tool. The other options each name a single result.
quests.whyThisTitle: The single shared calendar explains each benefit the passage lists.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Moving day goes faster when boxes are labeled. Write the room name and a short list of contents on two sides of each box. Put a colored sticker on boxes that should be opened first, such as kitchen and bathroom items. The movers then know where to carry each box, and you can find what you need right away.
options: How to Choose Colored Stickers for Gifts
Labeling Boxes for an Easy Move
Hiring Movers for a New Apartment
quests.correctAnswer: Labeling Boxes for an Easy Move
quests.hint: Ask how each piece of advice makes the day easier.
quests.explanation: Room names, contents lists, and stickers are all labeling methods. The other titles mention things that appear only as small examples.
quests.whyThisTitle: The room names, the lists, and the stickers are all ways of labeling, and the passage says why that helps.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Many banks offer savings accounts for teenagers. A parent usually helps open the account, and there is often no monthly fee. The account pays a small amount of extra money, called interest, every year. Saving a little each month lets a teenager watch the total grow.
options: Earning Money from a First Job
Paying Monthly Bank Fees on Accounts
quests.hint: Look for the type of account and the group of people it is meant for.
quests.explanation: Parent help, no monthly fee, and interest are features of one kind of account. Interest is explained, but only as one of those features.
quests.whyThisTitle: The features listed all describe a teen-friendly savings account.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Trail signs help hikers stay safe. Colored marks on trees show which path to follow, and signs at each crossing list the distance to the next stop. A map board near the entrance shows all routes and warns about steep parts. Reading the signs before you begin can prevent getting lost.
options: Painting Marks on Trees and Rocks
Getting Lost in a Forest Without a Map
Choosing Hiking Boots for Steep Paths
quests.hint: Think about the purpose of each sign that is described.
quests.explanation: Marks, crossing signs, and the map board are all guides for hikers. The painted trees and the risk of getting lost are only parts of the story.
quests.whyThisTitle: Every kind of sign in the passage helps hikers find their way, and the title covers all of them.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: For a job interview, plan to arrive fifteen minutes early. Check the route the day before, so a traffic delay does not surprise you. Bring a copy of your résumé and a pen, and turn your phone off before you walk in. Being ready in small ways shows the interviewer that you take the job seriously.
quests.hint: Notice that none of the advice is about what to say. What is it about?
quests.explanation: Arriving early, checking the route, and turning off the phone are all about readiness. A title about résumés or answers would miss that.
quests.whyThisTitle: The advice is all about practical readiness on the day of the interview.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: A rain barrel sits beneath the drainpipe of Mr. Wu's house. It collects water from the roof, and he uses it to water his flowers. In a dry month, he still has water without turning on the tap. The barrel cost little and lowers his water bill.
options: Painting a Drainpipe on the House
Paying a Monthly Water Bill on Time
quests.hint: Ask where the water comes from and where it goes.
quests.explanation: The barrel gathers water from the roof and supplies the garden. Bills and flowers are both connected, but only as effects of the barrel.
quests.whyThisTitle: The barrel, the roof water, and the lower bill are all part of collecting rainwater.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Every second Friday, a café in the city center hosts a language exchange. People sit at tables marked for different languages and talk for ten minutes at a time. Then a bell rings and everyone moves to a new table. Beginners say it is the easiest way to practice with real speakers.
options: Practicing Languages at a Café Meetup
Ringing a Bell to Change Tables
Opening a Café in the City Center
quests.correctAnswer: Practicing Languages at a Café Meetup
quests.hint: Ask what people gain from the event, not just how it is organized.
quests.explanation: The bell and the tables are how the event works, but its point is conversation practice. The title should capture both the place and the purpose.
quests.whyThisTitle: The rotating tables and short conversations all serve the goal of speaking practice.
